aisec: Swiss authorities confirmed AI-agent-driven intrusions succeeded in four of five confirmed attacks, including on critical infrastructure operators, showing agentic attacks are now a real-world threat.
Mitel MiCollab zero-days were exploited before Mitel's advisory in suspected AI-assisted extortion attacks, hinting that AI may be shrinking exploitation timelines.
Commentary urges current, operational security measures over presentation metrics as attackers move at AI speed; a threat roundup also flags AI server hijacking and malicious extensions.
ai: OpenAI fixed a bug that had wrongly discounted GPT-6.2 usage, so users now hit limits 40% faster; Nvidia also paused server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries amid export-control pressure.
Forty-two state attorneys general are trying to stop Character.AI from selling user chat histories in bankruptcy, highlighting privacy risks of AI conversation data.
Hugging Face posts cover Nemotron 3.5 Parse, a llama.cpp benchmark dashboard for AMD hardware, multi-agent systems, and video generation on Trainium3 with LTX-2.5.
cyber: Actively exploited flaws dominate: Drupal takeover bugs (including an incomplete installer patch), a critical Juniper Session Smart Conductor root-command flaw, and ten CISA KEV additions spanning Mitel, Juniper, Vates and Danfoss.

Developer-account and supply-chain attacks continue: 1Password reported a GitHub account breach exposing customer data and source code, PolinRider poisoned over 7,600 GitHub repositories, and 13 malicious NuGet packages targeted .NET developers.

Credential and email theft campaigns persist: GoodGuys fake-interview phishing, Remus and SYS01 browser-extension infostealers targeting Gmail and Outlook, while FIFA disclosed a breach and Iranian actors target Cyprus.
